_comment: Surface biomes and how they lie across the width. climate: the width runs cold (x = 0) to hot; orders are the ways the biomes can lie along it, one picked per world, each one naming every enabled biome once. share = [lo, hi] fraction of the width, drawn per world and normalised; no biome ends below min_share. seam = how far a border's skin and rock interleave, ramp = how far its height profile blends, both as a fraction of the width clamped to tiles. Rows: top, road, soil, stone are tile names (road: what a road between towns is surfaced with here), soil_wall and stone_wall wall names (stone reaches from the soil to a little under the surface band). soil_depth = [lo, hi] tiles. snow: top turns to this tile above a fraction of the surface band. map_color: tools/worldmap.gd. height: base = lift as a fraction of the surface band; big, mid, fine scale the world's noise (1 = the old meadow); ridge = sharp peaks, dune = short swells, both 0-1; step = most tiles between neighbouring columns (1 walks: a body steps up 1 tile; 2 asks for jumps, and a road cannot follow it without a flight of stairs).

orders.name: meltwater
orders.doc: Cold woods, the range, its melt pooling in the fens below, then grass drying out into desert.

orders.name: rain_shadow
orders.doc: Cold woods running down to fens and grass, and a range that keeps the rain from the desert behind it.

underground._doc: Regions of the underground biomes in the deeps and the nadir (core/world/worldgen/stage_deep.gd). A world narrower than min_world has none. bands: per band, the regions laid along it; each kind gets one region per `every` tiles of width (at least one), its width drawn from share (a fraction of the world's width) and clamped to tiles; the plain underdark fills the gaps (at least gap tiles each, margin kept at both ends of the world). seam = columns over which two neighbours' rock interleaves. regions: per biome its rock (replaces slate and stone in the band), floor (the top of rock under open air), wall (behind), glow (a light tile on floors, `every` columns on average; hang: also from ceilings), map_color (tools/worldmap.gd and the world map), and its own cave shape: round (domes: per `per` cells of region, radius r), angular (cellular chambers: freq, cut = the share of cells opened, rim = rock kept between them), lake (lake: the basin), tube (lava tubes in the low nadir with pools: pool width, bridge_over = pools this wide get a lava bridge, every = columns between pools).
